look_here_first: GREEN SPRANGLETOP: look for a usually PERENNIAL, often robust bunch with relatively broad bluish-green blades and a terminal head of about 2–15 long slender branches, frequently widely spreading or gently drooping. Branches carry spikelets mostly on ONE side. Then examine ONE mature 4–12 mm spikelet at 10–20×: commonly 4–13 florets (count inside one spikelet), with fairly blunt or NOTCHED, generally awnless or minutely pointed lemmas ~3.5–5 mm long. At the blade–sheath junction verify a SHORT MEMBRANOUS ligule with a fringed margin; in lower sheaths look for optional HIDDEN self-pollinating (cleistogamous) flowers. A flowering-head photo alone cannot prove florets, notches, ligule or hidden heads.

best_field_traits: PERENNIAL: typically stout bunchgrass with a lasting tough base, sometimes locally producing basal tillers; do not infer a root system from a cut stem.

PANICLE BRANCHES: usually about 2–15 slender, long, often widely spreading or nodding branches arranged along a main flowering axis; spikelets on mostly ONE side (secund). Inflorescence branch count is supporting, not uniquely diagnostic.
SPIKELETS: about 4–12 mm long, 4–13 florets PER INDIVIDUAL SPIKELET; count florets on the rachilla, not spikelets on different branches. Fertile florets may spread widely at maturity.
LEMMA: usually ~3.5–5 mm long, 3-veined, often hairy toward lower margins; tip broad, nearly square/obtuse to shallowly notched, awnless or with a tiny mucro, NOT a long threeawn bristle.
LIGULE: actual short membranous inside blade/sheath junction with a fringed/ciliate upper edge; genus treatment typically 0.5–1.5 mm, Flora of North America sometimes 1–2 mm.

SECONDARY HEADS: may produce cleistogamous (closed, self-pollinating) panicles enclosed LOW in leaf sheaths. Seeing one strongly supports ID; failing to find one on a single stalk does not rule species out.
Older names LEPTOCHLOA DUBIA / DIPLACHNE DUBIA are synonyms for the same plant. State-wide nativity or taxonomic flags were NOT newly audited in this visual upgrade.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: FULL HABIT: same individual photographed from tough perennial crown (with any basal tillers) to flowering head; add a centimeter ruler and note if stolons are present.
PANICLE: entire 2–15 branch flowering head with at least one branch showing its mostly one-sided spikelet attachment and where each branch arises along the main axis.
SPIKELET 10–20×: mm ruler beside an intact 4–12 mm spikelet, glumes and rachilla visible so 4–13 FLORETS can be individually counted.
LEMMA 20×: separate a mature 3.5–5 mm lemma and show its approximately flat/square, often shallowly two-notched tip, hair placement and any tiny mucro; do not claim a long awn.
TRUE COLLAR: unfold a blade and measure membranous ligule with finely fringed apex, showing the actual blade/sheath junction (2013 treatment 0.5–1.5 mm; some regional accounts 1–2 mm).
LOW SHEATHS: on the same plant, document an enclosed cleistogamous flowering head when present; absence in one sheath is not a negative ID.
MATCHED COMPARISON: Dinebra panicea subsp. mucronata full annual plant plus 2–4 mm 2–4-flowered mature spikelet, both shot at the same scale as Disakisperma.
crew_field_check: Trace a WHOLE rooted individual, not just a detached panicle: green sprangletop normally perennial, annual Dinebra has much finer panicle branches.
Observe the side of a mature flowering branch where spikelets line up. Under magnification, count individual florets inside ONE measured mature spikelet.
Look closely for broad square/obtuse often NOTCHED lemma tip and a genuinely fringed membranous ligule, and optionally a hidden secondary flowering head in a lower sheath.

Compare Dinebra on spikelet LENGTH and floret COUNT as well as habit: Disakisperma 4–12 mm and 4–13 florets, Dinebra commonly ~2–4 mm and 2–4 florets; counts can overlap, so don't decide from four alone.
Two new credited Commons photos show the real species from west Texas but do not demonstrate invisible microscopic anatomy; only mark what is actually visible.

comparisons.key_distinctions: DINEBRA PANICEA subsp. MUCRONATA (mucronate sprangletop): generally a slender ANNUAL with MANY fine ascending branches, tiny ~2–4 mm spikelets with typically 2–4 florets and a much smaller lemma; Green sprangletop is a usually larger PERENNIAL with about 2–15 often widely spreading branches and ~4–12 mm spikelets with 4–13 florets. Both may bear four-flowered spikelets: measure the actual mature spikelet AND inspect rooted habit before deciding. DIPLACHNE FUSCA (bearded sprangletop) can also have long spreading branches; its ligule tends to be much longer and pointed (often ~2–8 mm), and lemma tip shape differs, so confirm with a microscope. Old Leptochloa dubia and Diplachne dubia refer to the same green sprangletop taxon, not new cards. Do not mistake a single branch of the panicle for a whole spikelet.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Intact rooted plant, mature spikelet with scale and 10–20×
field_matrix.this_species: Usually perennial, ~2–15 sometimes spreading branches; spikelets ~4–12 mm with 4–13 florets
field_matrix.look_alike: Usually slender annual, many much finer branches; spikelets ~2–4 mm with ~2–4 florets
field_matrix.quick_rule: Four florets overlaps; branch shape alone does not decide. Compare mature spikelet size AND roots.

field_matrix.where_to_look: True membranous ligule length/shape, dissected mature lemma tip
field_matrix.this_species: Short ~0.5–1.5 mm ciliate-fringed membrane, blunt/commonly notched lemma, occasionally hidden low-sheath panicles
field_matrix.look_alike: Often longer more pointed 2–8 mm membranous ligule and more acute lemma tip, hidden low-sheath inflorescence absent in regional key
field_matrix.quick_rule: Don't use branch spread alone; the ligule and mature lemma provide the better distinction.

field_matrix.where_to_look: A mature spikelet and its branching context
field_matrix.this_species: Relatively few longer, one-sided branch axes with larger multiple-flowered spikelets; broad/obtuse lemma tips
field_matrix.look_alike: Many species have loose multi-branched panicles and spikelets with multiple florets; compare glumes, floret attachment and lemma tips
field_matrix.quick_rule: An airy panicle with several florets is not proof of either genus.

visual_comparison.memory_rule: PERENNIAL BUNCH + 2–15 OFTEN SPREADING ONE-SIDED BRANCHES + ONE 4–12 mm 4–13-FLORET SPIKELET + BLUNT/NOTCHED LEMMA points to green sprangletop. Dinebra often annual, finer-branched, with ~2–4 mm fewer-flowered spikelets.

measured_diagnostic_key.habit: Mostly perennial tufted or occasionally stoloniferous; document rooted crown rather than assuming perennial from a clipped flowering stem.
measured_diagnostic_key.terminal_panicle_cm: 10–45 long, 3–25 wide; raceme-like unilateral branches commonly 5–15
measured_diagnostic_key.spikelets_mm: 4–12, 4–13 florets, usually nearly sessile on unilateral branches
measured_diagnostic_key.lemma_mm: 3.5–5.0, usually 3-veined, often hairy on margins/below, apex sometimes shallowly bifid, awnless or minutely mucronate
measured_diagnostic_key.cleistogamy: Additional closed-flowering spikelets may be hidden in LOWER leaf sheaths; photograph on the same plant without claiming absence when not found.

look_alike_field_key.compare: Generally annual with 2–4(–5) florets per much smaller 2–4 mm spikelet and lemma about 0.9–1.7 mm in regional descriptions. Check rooted annual base, glumes, and true floret count; don't infer species from thin one-sided branches alone.
Require mature lemma length, floret count, ligule, and hidden lower-sheath inflorescences; retain Disakisperma sp. if structures are missing.
